# Help: PitchBook API

Find information about PitchBook’s API solution and discover how it can meet your business needs. Our API is a separate offering from the PitchBook Platform that requires a standalone contract agreement.

### Jump to

  * Overview
  * Use cases
  * How the API works

Overview

PitchBook’s API solution allows you to call specific PitchBook data into your internal business systems on demand. This flexible solution means you have access to PitchBook’s expansive database. It’s the ideal integration for CRM enrichment, allowing you to extract data on an ad-hoc basis that meets the needs of your organization.

You can explore a specific entity and retrieve valuable data, and the API solution enables you to apply specific criteria, such as location and industry, to drill down into the businesses you discover.


Use cases

The API is a good solution if:

  * Your scope and data points are subject to change frequently.
  * You require a near-instant population of data.
  * You perform ad-hoc research.
  * You want to see past and present financial data.
  * RESTful API is a system requirement.


How the API works

Accessing the API
The PitchBook API is a RESTful implementation that most HTTP clients can easily access in your chosen language or via a web browser. Every call will use the same base URL: https://api.pitchbook.com

Available data points
The API solution offers a variety of relational endpoints, including financing details, deal stock information, as well as AI-powered VC exit predictor data. See the full list from our API Endpoints Overview document.

Create your API connection
To start your API connection, you will need to send a request directly to our Direct Data team through this link.

Or if you’re a PitchBook client, you can also head to the Plugins & Apps section from the My PitchBook section of the left-hand sidebar on the PitchBook Platform and choose PitchBook API.

Image: Plugins and apps section of left-hand side-bar.jpg

From this section on the platform, you can test specific endpoints. This section on PitchBook also allows you to reach out to our Direct Data team to request access to the API.

## 

## Next steps

Our team will work with you to understand the insights and data you’re looking for and help you establish the API connection through an API key or authentication token. Available data for each entity type is packaged across several endpoints so you can map the data to your desired format and structure.

Image: 2024-globsl-g2-logo.svg

The platform is intuitive and easy-to-use and customer service is top-notch.”

—Steven Medley, Senior Market Intelligence Manager, Sidley Austin LLP

# Q. How do I access PitchBook?

Answered By: Lippincott Library

Last Updated: Aug 31, 2026     Views: 63234

### Access

Use the Penn Libraries' PitchBook link to access PitchBook.

Note: Accessing PitchBook will give the company your first name, last name, and Penn email.

### Plugins & Apps

To download the PitchBook Chrome Extension or Excel Plug-in:

  1. Log in to your PitchBook account
  2. Use the sidebar menu to select My PitchBook > Plugins & Apps.
  3. If you are prompted to log in after installation, choose Sign in with SSO, then enter your Penn or school email address.

These features are not included in our subscription:

  * PitchBook mobile app
  * PitchBook API

### Downloads

Individual users are subject to download limits of 10 daily/25 monthly rows of company, deal or fund data, as well as 10 daily/25 monthly rows of people data. If your download needs exceed those limits, please contact the librarians at the Lippincott Library (lippincott@wharton.upenn.edu). There are no download limits on public company fundamental data.

### Scraping & AI Browser Extensions

PitchBook prohibits scraping and will permanently revoke your access, immediately and automatically, upon detection. See the file below for details, including prohibited and acceptable uses.

Some PitchBook users have reported having access revoked after merely using PitchBook while running AI browser extensions (e.g.: Claude; ChatGPT). We recommend you disable these browser extensions before opening PitchBook or open PitchBook in a browser without extensions.

### Links & Files

  * PitchBook_Data_Scraping_Policy_for_Universities_-_Student.pdf

Contact your PitchBook account manager (or your organization's PitchBook administrator) to enable API access and issue an API key for your account. ...   * PitchBook Public API v2 documentation

#### 

Step 1: Obtain your API key

PitchBook API keys are provisioned as part of a paid API add-on rather than generated self-serve. Contact your PitchBook account manager (or your organization's PitchBook administrator) to enable API access and issue an API key for your account.

PitchBook also offers a test sandbox environment that uses the same base URL with a separate key. If you want to try the integration before running against production data, ask your account manager for a sandbox key as well.

Keep your API key secure

The API key grants access to your PitchBook data through the API. Treat it like a password and never expose it in client-side code or commit it to version control. If it is exposed, ask PitchBook to rotate it.

Configure the Frontegg portal

Once you have your API key, configure the integration in the Frontegg portal:

  1. Open the Frontegg portal and navigate to [ENVIRONMENT] → Integrations → PitchBook.
  2. Paste your API Key.
  3. Optionally set a Default currency — an ISO 4217 code (for example, `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `JPY`) applied to all monetary fields in responses. Leave it blank to use PitchBook's default.
  4. Click Save.

#### 

Keep your credentials secure

Never share or commit your API key to version control.

Additional resources

  * PitchBook data integrations overview
